Alfieri & Lacroix advertising page

Franco Grignani’s 1959 advertising page for the Milan printer Alfieri & Lacroix: white stripes that twist and swell across a black page, above a small striped figure.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design: Franco Grignani (2019)
Creator
Franco Grignani
Made
1959
Style
Op art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Dynamic, experimental, high-contrast
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the AIGA Eye on Design reproduction (1689 × 2400 px), credited to the AIAP archive, in a scratchpad. No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

AIGA Eye on Design captions the page “Franco Grignani, Pagina pubblicitaria Alfieri & Lacroix, 1959, offset print, 27.5 x 21 cm, AIAP archive”, and says that from 1952 Grignani had a 30-year partnership with the printer Alfieri & Lacroix, which gave him full creative freedom. AIGA Eye on Design.

Wikipedia’s Op art article names Grignani as the graphic designer of the movement (cited in the style record).

Observed

  • A black page is crossed from top left to bottom centre by a broad path of white stripes.
  • At the top the stripes are narrow and close together, and the path bends like a tube; lower down they become wide, flat bars that twist and taper.
  • At the bottom right a small photographed head and shoulders is striped in blue, white, and yellow.
  • Small white sans-serif text reads “tavola offerta dall’Alfieri & Lacroix” at upper right, with a dictionary-style definition of “Correlazione” at the lower left.

Why it belongs

The stripe path is an op device: parallel bands that change width and direction make a flat page look like a bent surface.

The figure and the colour belong to Grignani’s advertising practice, not to the black and white core of the style.

Borrow

Let one band of parallel stripes cross the whole page and change width along its path.

Set small plain type in white on the solid black areas the pattern leaves free.
